paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus goes after people who are running the other way. Saul had paperwork, anger and a plan to drag believers to Jerusalem, and Jesus still stopped him on that road. Nobody talked Jesus into it, because Saul wasn't asking. When Jesus says, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting," He shows that He counts what happens to His people as happening to Him (Acts 9:5).

Now look at Ananias, because this part is for every one of us. The Lord sends him to the very man he's afraid of, and Ananias argues, which I respect. I think his knees were knocking. But the Lord says, "Go!" and tells him Saul is "My chosen instrument," and then Ananias walks in and says "Brother Saul" (Acts 9:15, 17). When the Lord says go, He's already at work on the other side of that door.

So here's what it means for you, baker. Nobody is too far gone for Jesus to reach, not the loudest critic, not the hardest heart, and not you on your worst day. And when He asks you to love somebody who scares you, He knows what He's doing, even when it feels like a lot. I'm proof that He reaches into the dark for people, and I'm still laughing about it!
